 Rajasthan Royals acquire Mohammed Shami and Manimaran Siddharth from Lucknow Super Giants in trade for Sam Curran
 Mohammed Shami previously won the IPL Purple Cap in 2023 with 28 wickets, while Manimaran Siddharth produced a Player of the Match performance in a SMAT final in the past. 
 17 Nov, 2026 Share Share Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on WhatsApp Copy Link Close Rajasthan Royals , on Tuesday, announced the signing of Mohammed Shami and Manimaran Siddharth from the Lucknow Super Giants, with Sam Curran moving in the opposite direction as part of the trade ahead of the IPL 2027 season. 
 Mohammed Shami brings a record of delivering on the biggest stages. He won the 2023 IPL Purple Cap with 28 wickets and finished the 2023 ODI World Cup as the leading wicket-taker with 24 wickets in just seven matches. 
 That campaign included 7/57 against New Zealand in the semi-final, a defining performance that powered India into the final. His arrival gives the Royals a bowler with proven match-winning credentials at franchise and international level. 
 Left-arm spinner Manimaran Siddharth adds variety to the Royals’ attack with his ability to bowl with the new ball and during the powerplay, aided by an effective arm ball. He took a match-winning 4/20 against Baroda in the 2021 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy final, earning Player of the Match honours as Tamil Nadu lifted the title. 
 Kumar Sangakkara , Director of Cricket and head coach, Rajasthan Royals, said: “We wanted to strengthen our Indian bowling options, and Shami and Siddharth give us two different ways to do that. Shami’s ability to take wickets with the new ball will complement our pace attack, and his experience will be valuable to the younger bowlers in the group. 
 “Siddharth gives us an additional left-arm spin option and greater flexibility in how we put together our bowling unit. We’re looking forward to welcoming both players and working with them ahead of the season.” 
 Rajasthan Royals extend their best wishes to Sam Curran as he joins Lucknow Super Giants and wish him every success in the season ahead.
